scope: Bounded V12 methodological reading batch. Each record names the inspected unit, representation hash and omissions. Registration and reading are not independent review, model validation or permission to reproduce source text.

records.unit_label: SimPy 4.1 topical guides: Events, Process Interaction, Shared Resources, Time and Scheduling
records.access_method: Public HTTPS fetch; HTML text extracted with a script-only/style-only filter and whitespace normalisation
sections_read: Events: triggering events and process events
Process Interaction: sleep until woken up
Process Interaction: waiting for another process to terminate
Shared Resources: the basic concept of resources
Shared Resources: Resource, PriorityResource and PreemptiveResource
Time and Scheduling: event processing order and same-time events
records.omissions: Only four bounded topical guides were read. The API reference, examples, monitoring and real-time material were excluded. The guides describe a Python library, not a reference architecture or a measured system.
claims_supported: SimPy models time through scheduled events and processes events one after another even when several events share a timestamp.
Processes can wait for timeouts, other processes, or combinations of events, and can be interrupted.
Resource objects provide capacity-bounded acquisition with queueing, and priority or preemption variants exist.
Container and Store objects model level- and item-based shared state.
claims_not_supported: Any measured latency, throughput or capacity result
Any claim that SimPy's event order matches a particular production scheduler
Any claim about versions other than the inspected 4.1 documentation
records.limitations: Documentation inspection only; no SimPy code was executed in V12. The V12 engine is independently implemented and does not embed SimPy.

records.unit_label: Monte Carlo theory, methods and examples: Chapters 1-2 and Appendix A.6
records.access_method: Public HTTPS PDF fetch; pdftotext -layout text extraction and whitespace normalisation
sections_read: Chapter 1: introduction, traffic-model example, notation and outline
Chapter 2: accuracy of simple Monte Carlo
Chapter 2: error estimation and safe standard-error computation
Chapter 2: estimating probabilities, quantiles, ratios and random sample size
Appendix A.6: Sobol' indices, closed and total sensitivity indices, pick-freeze estimation and mean dimension
records.omissions: The unit is deliberately bounded to Chapters 1-2 and Appendix A.6. Variance-reduction chapters, MCMC, quasi-Monte Carlo and the remaining appendices were not read.
claims_supported: Simple Monte Carlo error decreases with the square root of the sample size under finite-variance assumptions.
A standard-error estimate supports approximate confidence intervals, but the guarantees depend on assumptions and can fail for heavy tails or dependent samples.
Sobol' indices decompose output variance by input subsets; first-order and total-effect indices answer different sensitivity questions.
Pick-freeze estimators use paired evaluations to estimate sensitivity indices.
claims_not_supported: Any claim that a particular V12 Monte Carlo run has converged without computing its error
Any coverage guarantee for a finite sample with unknown dependence
Any measured production distribution
records.limitations: Selected chapters only. The book is a methods reference; it does not validate any V12 model or its parameter values.

records.access_method: Public HTTPS PDF fetch; pdftotext -layout text extraction and whitespace normalisation
sections_read: Lecture 2: systems thinking, system dynamics definition and unintended consequences
Lecture 3: dynamic complexity, stocks and flows, hydraulic metaphor, integration and feedback
Lecture 4: negative feedback, exponential decay, explicit goals and adjustment time
records.omissions: Three lecture PDFs only. The broader course, its readings and its project material were not read.
claims_supported: Stocks are accumulations over time; inflows and outflows change them and the net flow is the rate of change of the stock.
Stocks decouple inflows and outflows and provide memory and inertia in a system.
Feedback loops, delays and nonlinearity can produce counterintuitive dynamics and policy resistance.
Simulation is used to explore how modeled socio-technical systems may behave under explicit assumptions.
claims_not_supported: Any empirical calibration of a socio-technical model
Any claim that a particular stock-and-flow model predicts a real system
Any organizational or sector-specific performance claim
records.limitations: Open courseware lecture slides only; no exercises, datasets or case measurements. The material motivates modeling but does not validate a V12 model.

records.unit_label: Verification and Validation of Simulation Models - full paper
records.version: Proceedings of the 2011 Winter Simulation Conference, paper 016
records.access_method: Public HTTPS PDF fetch; pdftotext -layout text extraction and whitespace normalisation
sections_read: Model-development paradigms and the verification/validation relationship
Validation techniques including degenerate tests, extreme-condition tests, sensitivity analysis and traces
records.omissions: The full paper text was read. The paper's references and the cited methods were not independently inspected.
claims_supported: Model verification concerns whether the computer program of the model is correct; model validation concerns whether the model is adequate for its intended purpose.
Validity is purpose- and domain-dependent, and a model change requires verification and validation again.
Validation can combine comparison to other models, degenerate tests, extreme-condition tests, historical data, internal validity, sensitivity analysis, traces and Turing tests.
Data validity, conceptual-model validity and operational validity are distinct concerns.
claims_not_supported: Any claim that a V12 model is valid for a real system
Any measured data quality assessment
Any certification, accreditation or regulatory acceptance
records.limitations: Methodological guidance only. The paper does not inspect any V12 model, dataset or run, and does not establish production readiness.

records.access_method: Public HTTPS fetch; HTML text extraction and whitespace normalisation
sections_read: Starting-point terms: wasGeneratedBy, used, wasInformedBy, wasStartedBy, wasEndedBy, wasInvalidatedBy, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith, actedOnBehalfOf
Expanded terms: primary and qualified influence relations
Qualified terms: generation, usage, communication, start, end, invalidation, derivation, attribution, association, delegation
records.omissions: Only sections 1-4 were inspected. The complete ontology examples, term index and linked documents were excluded.
records.representation_gap: The page is large and browser-rendered; section text was extracted without executing scripts. Links, diagrams and examples were not represented.
claims_supported: Provenance can be described with entities, activities and agents and with relations such as generation, use, derivation and attribution.
A qualified relation can carry additional details such as a role, time or plan.
Provenance descriptions can connect a produced artifact to the activity and inputs that produced it.
claims_not_supported: That V12 records conform to PROV-O or validate against its ontology
That PROV-O captures statistical correctness
That provenance alone establishes reproducibility
records.limitations: Vocabulary inspiration only. V12 uses a small subset of PROV-O concepts in its own JSON contract and does not claim conformance.

records.unit_label: MADR - Markdown Architectural Decision Records landing page and template guidance
records.access_method: Public HTTPS fetch; HTML text extraction and whitespace normalisation
sections_read: About MADR and the definition of an architectural decision
Using MADR in large projects and product developments
records.omissions: The landing page only. The linked template repository, releases, examples and tooling were not read.
claims_supported: MADR is a structured Markdown template for architectural decision records.
A record separates context and problem statement, considered options and decision outcome.
The project treats decision capture as lightweight, versionable documentation.
claims_not_supported: That MADR is the only valid decision-record format
That a MADR record proves a decision is correct
That V12 decision records are MADR-conformant
records.limitations: Format guidance only. V12 uses a compatible JSON-first structure and does not claim MADR conformance.

sections_not_read: Linked posts and unrelated site material
records.omissions: The full article was read. Linked posts and unrelated site pages were excluded.
claims_supported: Architecturally significant decisions can be recorded as short, modular documents.
A decision record should preserve context, the decision, its status and its consequences.
Small records are easier to keep current than a single large specification.
claims_not_supported: That a decision record is a substitute for measurement or review
That every decision must use one template
That V12 decision records are Nygard-format records
records.limitations: A practice article, not empirical evidence. V12 adapts the structure and states its own status and limits.

records.unit_label: Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research - full article
records.access_method: Public HTTPS fetch; HTML text extraction and whitespace normalisation
sections_read: Examples and rationale for tracked inputs, versioned scripts, recorded parameters, archived environments and provenance
records.omissions: The article text was read; supporting files, references and figures were excluded.
claims_supported: Reproducible computational research benefits from tracking input data, versioning scripts, recording parameters and archiving the computational environment.
A record should allow another person to rerun the analysis and obtain the same result.
Manual steps and untracked state are risks to reproducibility.
claims_not_supported: That following the rules guarantees reproducibility
That V12 is reproducible on every platform
That a hash alone proves correctness
records.limitations: Guidance article only. V12 implements a bounded subset: canonical inputs, seeds, engine version, hashes and replay tests.

records.access_method: Public HTTPS PDF fetch; pdftotext -layout text extraction and whitespace normalisation
sections_read: Clause 3: basic concepts and the measurement model
Clause 4: evaluating standard uncertainty from Type A and Type B components
Clause 5: determining combined standard uncertainty and expanded uncertainty
records.omissions: Selected clauses only. The annexes, detailed examples and later clauses were excluded.
records.representation_gap: The PDF was extracted as layout text; equations, symbols and figures may be degraded. Clause meaning was read from surrounding prose, not from a symbol-level transcription.
claims_supported: A measurement result includes a measured value and an uncertainty, and the measurement model relates input quantities to the output quantity.
Standard uncertainty can be combined from components, and an expanded uncertainty defines a coverage interval at a stated coverage probability.
Reporting uncertainty requires the measured value, the uncertainty, the coverage factor and the coverage probability.
claims_not_supported: That V12 inputs are metrologically calibrated
That a synthetic parameter uncertainty is a measured Type A or Type B component
That V12 conforms to JCGM 100
records.limitations: Vocabulary only. V12 uses uncertainty language to separate assumed, measured, derived and unknown inputs; it does not perform a metrological uncertainty budget.

records.unit_label: Statistical Analysis with Little's Law - selected sections
records.access_method: Public HTTPS PDF fetch; pdftotext -layout text extraction and whitespace normalisation
records.omissions: Selected sections only. Proofs, case data and simulation details were not independently reproduced.
records.representation_gap: The PDF was extracted as layout text; equations and symbols may be degraded. Prose meaning was used, not symbol-level transcription.
claims_supported: Little's Law relates long-run average number in system, arrival rate and average time in system under stated conditions.
Finite-window measurements are not the same as long-run averages and can carry edge bias.
Batch means can support confidence intervals for simulation output.
claims_not_supported: Any measured V12 queue behavior
Any claim that a finite sample satisfies the long-run law exactly
Any production capacity conclusion
records.limitations: Selected sections only; the paper is methodological and does not validate the V12 engine or its scenarios.
